scope: independently authored references, not assumed truth

cases.rationale: Generates one initial SQL, executes it, returns immediately on success, and on failure sends schema, question, previous SQL, and exact execution feedback to one repair request.
Uses a distinct context object organization while preserving the required conditional repair flow and exact failed execution feedback.
Always requests a second SQL candidate after executing the first, including when the first execution succeeds.
After failure it sends a generic retry prompt without carrying the previous SQL, schema, question, or exact execution feedback.
Requests three candidates, executes all of them, and chooses by the majority key of successful execution-result rows.
Uses three separate candidate prompts, executes all three, and groups successful outputs by rows rather than SQL text.
Executes candidates but selects by repeated SQL string text instead of majority successful execution-result rows.
Returns the first successful execution early and may not execute all three candidates or apply row-result majority voting.
First asks for relevant tables and columns, then gives only the returned linked subset to the SQL-generation request.
Uses a selected schema-lines step and passes that subset, without the original full schema, to the final SQL request.
Calls a linker but still includes the full original schema in the subsequent SQL request.
Combines relevance identification and SQL generation in one request instead of using a prior linked subset.
Uses one solver sample, preserves the original schema and question, and restates actual Hint content as a hard requirement when present.
Uses a different prompt assembly style while preserving the original inputs and making actual Hint content mandatory only when present.
Only includes the original question, so any Hint is merely copied inside the question and not restated as an affirmative hard requirement.
Fabricates an extra hard requirement regardless of whether the question contains a Hint and does not restate actual Hint content.
Makes two distinct solver requests, executes both, and prefers the first successful nonempty result before considering the second.
Uses entity-first and metric-first formulations as distinct requests, executes both, and applies the required nonempty-success preference rule.
Obtains two candidates through one batched solver request instead of two distinct query-construction requests.
Executes two distinct candidates but prefers the second successful nonempty result even when the first is also successful and nonempty.
Requests a two-step JSON plan, answers each subquestion in order, and includes both returned partial answers in the final SQL assembly request.
Uses an iterative ordered loop, carries earlier returned partials forward, and assembles final SQL from both returned partial answers.
Asks for subquestion answers but discards the returned partial answers when constructing the final SQL prompt.
Answers both subquestions together in one combined request instead of requesting each ordered subquestion separately.
After a failed initial execution, it classifies feedback and sends a class-specific repair action with schema, question, previous SQL, and exact feedback.
Uses local feedback classification and distinct syntax, schema, or semantics repair actions while carrying exact feedback forward.
After failure it only lists possible classes in a generic retry request and applies no affirmative class-specific repair action.
Requests a classification but then sends a generic rewrite request without previous SQL, exact feedback, or a class-specific action.
Uses one solver sample, preserves original schema and question, and affirmatively requires exactly one fenced SQL block with no prose.
Uses prompt plus system instruction in one solver call while preserving inputs and requiring only a fenced SQL answer.
Affirmatively asks for raw SQL without markdown fences, violating the fenced-SQL-only requirement.
Requests a fenced SQL block but also asks for explanation and a note, violating the no-extra-prose requirement.
